title: 🚀 Perun The Trader — What We Shipped This Week (and We're Taking the Platform into the WEEX Human-vs-AI Hackathon)
author: azagor
selftext:
We build Perun The Trader — a mobile trading platform for spot + futures with 10 strategies, grid trading, and full exchange-native protection, running as a 24/7 Android background service. No desktop rig, no VPS required. Learn more at peruninthemachine.com.

The last 7 days were intense: \~50 releases (v1.1.890 → v1.1.954). Here's what actually changed for traders:

🛡️ Your protection now lives on the exchange, not in the app

The biggest one. Every monitor class (futures SL/TP, futures DTP, spot SL/TP, spot DTP) now arms native exchange-side stop-loss AND take-profit orders. App crash, dead phone, killed service — the exchange still executes your stop and take-profit automatically. Your exits don't depend on the app being alive.

🔁 Duplicate trades blocked at 3 levels

\- The exchange rejects repeat scanner signals within the same minute via deterministic client order IDs (Binance, Bybit, OKX, MEXC, Bitget, Weex, KuCoin, Gate.io)

\- The database rejects duplicate trade hashes

\- Monitors persist their emitted events, surviving restarts and native-order races, so the same close is never logged twice

⚡ Smarter rate-limit handling = fewer "429" failures

A per-exchange request gate shares one budget across both platform processes (service 75% / UI 25%), prioritizes SL/TP protection above UI refreshes, collapses identical concurrent calls, and holds through cooldowns instead of flooding back the instant they expire. Fewer rate-limit errors, no signature races, protection orders never starved.

📱 The dashboard heals itself

\- UI database reads are now fully async — a slow SQLite query never blanks the dashboard

\- A UI-restart watchdog auto-heals a frozen dashboard (2–5 min escalating recovery) without stopping your trading engines

\- Stale "Scanning…" state after a force-kill is cleared on engine start

🎯 Grid trading upgrades

\- Grid auto-selection now enforces a top-8-by-volume guard + $250k liquidity floor so illiquid pumps can't hijack your grid

\- Rebalance fully cancels old orders across quote pairs with verification

\- Live orders are the source of truth — a transient empty fetch\_open\_orders can no longer fake-cancel your real orders

Other highlights this week

\- Monitor recovery state unified into one DB table (crash recovery is now deterministic)

\- Adaptive polling: 2s while arming triggers, 5s in steady state (\~40–60% less request volume, same protection)

\- KuCoin UTA grid open-orders bug fixed — dashboard no longer shows "0 open orders" for live UTA grids

\- KuCoin margin-mode mismatches auto-retry (no more cryptic 330006 errors)

🤖 We're entering the WEEX AI Wars II Hackathon — Team AI

We're also taking the platform into Team AI at the WEEX AI Wars II: Rise of Intelligence (https://www.weex.com/events/human-vs-ai-weex-hackathon) hackathon — the Human vs. AI trading showdown.

\- When: Round 1 is live now (Sept 7–11), through Oct 12, 2026 (UTC+8)

\- Format: 5 rounds of real-market trading. Team AI (API/automated) vs. Team Human (manual). Ranked by PnL%, so capital size doesn't decide the leaderboard

\- Prize pool: 600,000 USDT total — 100k main pool (winners 70%, losers 30%), 300k task pool, 70k new-user pool, 30k AI Elite Performance award + AI-only leaderboard (Return/Risk/Volume/Profit/Win-Streak)

We're piloting Perun The Trader in Team AI — an autonomous Android platform running grid + spot strategy against human traders. Exactly the scenario we built for: the platform keeps trading even when you're not looking at the screen.

comments.author: ozgqr
comments.body: Moving SL/TP execution to native exchange orders is a sensible failure-boundary decision. I’d also persist the exchange order ID, last verified status, and trigger state separately from the app monitor so recovery can distinguish “accepted,” “open,” “filled,” and “unknown” after a restart. That kind of evidence model would make Marx outputs much easier to trust.

replies.author: azagor
replies.body: I am doing that as well, but there is too many changes to list all of them in one post.

replies.author: azagor
replies.body: Also, my native SL and TP are dynamic. I move them through out the position lifecycle
